title: Class marks report in C

authoring.author: Parikshaa content team
authoring.originality: Written for Parikshaa: our own project brief, code, tests and rubric for class marks report in c, examples, code, quiz and explanations; no text from any site, book or course.

brief: A class teacher wants a quick report from a list of marks: how many students, the average, the topper, how many got each grade, and a ranked top list. Build it in C with a struct for the class, a header that declares the operations and a source file that implements them.
requirements: At most 100 students; marks are 0-100; a name can be added once.
STATS prints the count, the average to one decimal and the highest scorer (the first entered on a tie).
GRADES counts A (80+), B (60-79), C (40-59) and F (below 40).
TOP k lists the k best by marks, ties by name in alphabetical order.
io_protocol:
| Command | Prints |
|---|---|
| `ADD <name> <marks>` | `added <name>`, `error: class full`, `error: marks must be 0-100`, `error: <name> already added` or `error: name too long` |
| `STATS` | `count <n>, average <x.x>, highest <name> <marks>` or `no students` |
| `GRADES` | `A <n> B <n> C <n> F <n>` |
| `TOP <k>` | `<rank>. <name> <marks>` for up to k students, or `no students` |

Names are one word, at most 31 characters. Anything else: `error: bad command <line>`.

milestones.title: Adding and statistics
hints: Check the three errors in the order of the return codes.
Sum into a long and divide as double for the average.
Use > (not >=) so the first student keeps a tie for the top.

milestones.title: Grade counts
hints: Test the highest band first: 80, then 60, then 40.

milestones.title: Ranking
milestones.instructions: Implement `class_ranking`: sort indexes by marks descending, then name ascending.
hints: Insertion sort is fine for 100 students and easy to get right.
strcmp(a, b) < 0 means a comes first alphabetically.

rubric.criterion: Hidden tests pass: every command prints exactly the expected output.
The header declares the operations and the struct; main.c only calls them; no global variables in marks.c; buffers are bounded.
Readable names, small functions and clear error handling (AI feedback, advice only).

extensions: Print the median as well as the average.
